title: Reading a y-intercept
source: Theory P1-3.3 Quick check 1 (intercept 3); new integer intercepts
stem: A straight line has equation \(y=2x+{c|int}\). What is the \(y\)-intercept?

steps.name: A
steps.note: A equals c. Original c=3 gives 3.

title: y-intercept from two points with gradient 2
source: Theory P1-3.3 Quick check 2 (intercept 2); new points on y=2x+b
stem: The points \(A(1, {y1|int})\) and \(B(3, {y2|int})\) lie on a straight line. What is the \(y\)-intercept of the line \(AB\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: The gradient is 2, so \(y-{y1|int}=2(x-1)\) and the \(y\)-intercept is {A|int}.
steps.note: Points lie on y=2x+b, so the intercept is b. Original b=2 gives 2.

title: A negative y-intercept
source: Theory P1-3.3 Quick check 3 (intercept -3); new negative intercepts
stem: A straight line has equation \(y=x-{c|int}\). What is the \(y\)-intercept?

title: Equation of the line AB

source.note: 9709/12/F/M/23 Question 11(a) only [2]. Official QP and official MS. Later parts omitted.

stem:
This question is 9709/12/F/M/23 Question 11(a) only, taken from the official QP.

The diagram shows the curve with equation x = y² + 1. The points A (5, 2) and B (2, −1) lie on the curve.

(a) Find an equation of the line AB. [2]

steps.name: M
steps.note: Official MS: M1, expect 1, must be from dy/dx differences.

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: An equation of \(AB\) is \(y-2=1(x-5)\) or \(y+1=1(x-2)\), so \(y=x-3\).
steps.note: Official MS: A1, OE. Expect y=x-3. Independent: gradient 3/3=1, y-2=1(x-5), y=x-3.

contexts.note: Stem taken from the official QP PDF (UCLES 2023), Question 11(a) only. Official MS reproduced mark by mark. Paper/self-mark.
